text: First, meet the Moon. It's about three thousand four hundred and seventy kilometres across, roughly a quarter of the width of Earth. It's the fifth biggest moon in the whole solar system. On average, it sits about three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometres away. That gap is so big, you could line up every other planet in the solar system inside it. And it's slowly drifting away, about three point eight centimetres every year. That's about how fast your fingernails grow.
